guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our modest disagreement with the market begins with Auburn’s ability to create scoring opportunities. Our matchup numbers rate that part of Auburn’s offense more favorably than Tennessee’s ability to prevent those chances, which gives us a path to the underdog staying competitive even if Tennessee is the stronger team overall.

The concern is what happens on the other side. Tennessee has been highly effective at generating and finishing scoring opportunities, converting all 11 red-zone trips through its first three games and scoring 10 touchdowns. We view that as supporting evidence rather than a guarantee, especially because the available guide predates Tennessee’s game against Texas.

For us, the case for Auburn is offset by two meaningful matchup problems: Tennessee can finish drives, and Auburn may struggle to move the ball efficiently through the air. That leaves our model slightly more favorable to Auburn than the market without creating enough value at the current price, so we remain on the pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Auburn’s passing offense against Tennessee’s pass defense. Tennessee allowed only 151 passing yards per game through its first three contests, conceded just two completions of at least 20 yards and recorded 13 sacks. If Auburn cannot avoid pressure and produce enough chunk gains, its advantage in creating scoring opportunities may not translate into points. That tension is the clearest reason we see an argument for Auburn without finding a wager.

recent_game.fact: Tennessee improved to 3-0 with a 42-9 win over Kennesaw State on Sept. 19, rushing for 268 yards and holding Kennesaw State to three field goals and no touchdowns.
Against Kennesaw State, Daune Morris rushed 14 times for 116 yards and a 42-yard touchdown, recording his first career 100-yard rushing game.
Faizon Brandon completed 18 of 26 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown against Kennesaw State and added 47 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries.
Tennessee held Kennesaw State to 102 rushing yards; Arion Carter had eight tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss, while Edwin Spillman had five tackles and a forced fumble.

opponent_notes.fact: Tennessee's schedule lists Auburn as a home game on Oct. 3, 2026, with the kickoff window not yet finalized in this guide.
Auburn head coach Alex Golesh previously worked under Josh Heupel as offensive coordinator and tight ends coach at UCF in 2020 and at Tennessee in 2021-22.

quarterback.fact: True freshman Faizon Brandon won Tennessee's starting quarterback job in preseason camp and was officially named the starter on Aug. 24.
Through three starts, Brandon had accounted for nine touchdowns—six passing and three rushing—and had not thrown an interception in 64 attempts.
Brandon had thrown at least one touchdown pass in each of Tennessee's first three games and had two games with both a passing and rushing touchdown.
Brandon became the youngest quarterback to start a game in Tennessee history when he started the Sept. 5 opener against Furman at 18 years, three months and four days old.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris were both averaging more than 70 rushing yards per game through three games: Bishop 95.3 and Morris 78.0.
Bishop had 286 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns through three games, including 175 yards after contact.
Mike Matthews led Tennessee through three games with 10 receptions and 189 receiving yards and was tied for the team lead with two receiving touchdowns.
Braylon Staley had caught a touchdown pass in consecutive games against Georgia Tech and Kennesaw State.
Wide receiver Radarious Jackson made his first career start against Kennesaw State.

Tennessee's primary offensive-line combination in its two most recent games was David Sanders Jr. at left tackle, Wendell Moe Jr. at left guard, Sam Pendleton at center, Sham Umarov at right guard and Jesse Perry at right tackle.
Tennessee had eight offensive linemen with FBS starting experience, combining for 103 starts.

defensive_personnel.fact: Penn State transfer linebacker Amare Campbell led Tennessee with 17 tackles, including 11 solo tackles, through three games.
Penn State transfer defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam led Tennessee with 3.0 sacks and 5.5 tackles for loss through three games.
Penn State transfer safety Dejuan Lane had a team-high three passes defended and returned an interception 41 yards for a touchdown at Georgia Tech.

Senior linebacker Arion Carter returned against Georgia Tech after a one-game NCAA suspension and recorded eight tackles in each of his first two games back, with two sacks and two tackles for loss over that span.
Cornerback Kayin Lee transferred to Tennessee after starting 25 games in three seasons at Auburn; the guide states he did not allow a touchdown in 2025.
Defensive end Carson Gentle made his first career start against Kennesaw State.

coaching_changes.fact: Jim Knowles was named Tennessee's defensive coordinator on Dec. 11, 2025, after serving as Penn State's defensive coordinator in 2025.
Tennessee added Anthony Poindexter as co-defensive coordinator and secondary coach, Andrew Jackson as LEOs coach and Derek Jones as cornerbacks coach for 2026.
All five Tennessee offensive assistant coaches returned for 2026, including offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Joey Halzle.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Ethan Davis is out for the remainder of the 2026 season with a knee injury sustained at Georgia Tech in Week 2.
Cornerback Jadais Richard is out for the season after suffering an injury during the summer.
Arion Carter was described as fully healthy after offseason foot surgery and returned to action in Week 2 following a one-game NCAA suspension.

offensive_context.fact: Through three games, Tennessee averaged 47.7 points, 510.3 total yards and 298.7 rushing yards per game; its rushing average ranked first in the SEC and fourth nationally.
Tennessee exceeded 400 yards of total offense in each of its first three games and in 16 of its previous 17 regular-season games.
Tennessee converted all 11 of its red-zone opportunities through three games, scoring touchdowns on 10 of them.
Tennessee scored a touchdown on its opening offensive drive in each of its first three games, with every drive taking fewer than three-and-a-half minutes.
Tennessee outscored its first three opponents 44-0 in the second quarter and 86-10 across the second and third quarters.
Tennessee had a 36-2 record under Josh Heupel when rushing for at least 200 yards and had won 30 consecutive games when reaching that mark.

defensive_context.fact: Tennessee recorded 13 sacks through three games, ranking third nationally and second in the SEC.
Tennessee recorded 24 tackles for loss through three games, ranking tied for 10th nationally.
Opponents scored two offensive touchdowns on 33 drives against Tennessee through three games, a rate of 6.1 percent.
Tennessee allowed 151.0 passing yards per game through three games, the second-best mark in the SEC and 20th nationally.
Tennessee allowed only two pass plays of at least 20 yards and no pass play of at least 30 yards through three games.
Tennessee's defense did not allow a first-half touchdown in any of its first three games, and its starting defense surrendered only one touchdown over that span.

special_teams.fact: Louisville transfer Cooper Ranvier made all three field-goal attempts, including a long of 43 yards, and all 17 extra-point attempts in his first three games at Tennessee.
Justin Baker blocked a punt in Tennessee's Week 2 win at Georgia Tech.

other_relevant.fact: The guide's information reflects Tennessee at 3-0 before its Sept. 26 game against Texas, so it does not include the result, injuries or personnel developments from the game immediately preceding Auburn.
